πρὸς Θεὸν οἰκειότητος οἱ ἐξ Ἰσραὴλ, εἴρηται
σαφῶς, ἵνα δικαίᾳ ψήφῳ φαίνηται Θεὸς πανταχοῦ κεχρημένος. Ἔδει γὰρ, ἔδει τοὺς
τὴν εἰς Θεὸν ἀσέβειαν τιμήσαντας, ἔξω γενέσθαι τῆς παρ' αὐτοῦ φειδοῦς καὶ
ἀγάπης· τούς γε μὴν ἐξ ἀμαθίας τοῖς τῆς ἁμαρτίας βόθροις ἐνειλημμένους, καὶ ὑπὸ
χεῖρα πεσόντας διαβολικὴν, κατοικτειρῆσαι παρὰ τοῦ πάντων ∆ημιουργοῦ,
καλουμένους εἰς ἐπί- γνωσιν αὐτοῦ, καὶ εἰς τὸ τῆς ἀληθείας φῶς. Τοῦτο γάρ που καὶ
διὰ τοῦ πανσόφου Μωσέως εὑρίσκεται λέγων· Αὐτοὶ παρεζήλωσάν με ἐπ' οὐ θεοῖς,
παρ- ώξυνάν με ἐπὶ τοῖς γλυπτοῖς αὐτῶν. Κἀγὼ παραζη- λώσω αὐτοὺς ἐπ' οὐκ ἔθνει·
ἐπ' ἔθνει ἀσυνέτῳ παρ- οργιῶ αὐτούς. Ἔφη δέ που καὶ ὁ θεσπέσιος Μελῳδὸς, ὅτι
"6Παρεπίκραναν αὐτὸν ἐν τοῖς γλυπτοῖς αὐτῶν, καὶ ἐν τοῖς ἐπιτηδεύμασιν αὐτῶν
παρεζήλωσαν 70.880 αὐτόν· καὶ εἶδε Κύριος ὁ Θεὸς, καὶ ὑπερεῖδε, καὶ ἐξουδένωσε
σφόδρα τὸν Ἰσραήλ."6 Εἰ δὲ χρή τινα καὶ θεωρίαν πνευματικὴν τοῖς εἰρημένοις
ἐπενεγκεῖν, φυ- λαττόμεθα παγίδα διαβολικὴν εἰς νοῦν ἔχειν καὶ καρδίαν, καὶ τὰ ἐν
φαντασίαις λογισμῶν εἴδωλα πονηρὰ, καλοῦντα πρὸς ἀσέλγειαν καὶ εἰς ἐκτόπους
ἡδονὰς, ἵνα μὴ γενώμεθα τῷ Σατανᾷ, καὶ ἅρπαγμα δαιμονίων. Γέγραπται γὰρ, ὅτι
"6Ἐὰν πνεῦμα τοῦ ἐξουσιάζοντος ἀναβῇ ἐπὶ σὲ, τόπον σου μὴ ἀφῇς, ὅτι ἴαμα
καταπαύσει ἁμαρτίας μεγάλας."6 9Τίς ἐν ὑμῖν ἐνωτιεῖται ταῦτα; εἰσακούσατε εἰς
τὰ ἐπερχόμενα.9 Ἔθος τῇ θεοπνεύστῳ Γραφῇ τὸ ἀκουτίσασθαι λέ- γειν, ἐπὶ τοῦ μὴ
παρέργως, ἢ ἀτημελῶς, τὸν ἐπί γε τοῖς ἀναγκαίοις πράγμασι δέχεσθαι λόγον, νηφα-
λέως δὲ μᾶλλον, ὥστε καὶ εἰς νοῦν καὶ καρδίαν ἀπόθε- τον ἔχειν τὸ διηγγελμένον.
Ὁποῖόν ἐστι τὸ διὰ τῆς τοῦ Ψάλλοντος φωνῆς εἰρημένον· "6Ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ μου
ἔκρυψα τὰ λόγιά σου, ὅπως ἂν μὴ ἁμάρτω σοι."6 Γέγραπται γὰρ καὶ ἐν
τεσσαροκοστῷ καὶ ὀγδόῳ ψαλμῷ· "6Ἀκούσατε ταῦτα, πάντα τὰ ἔθνη, ἐνωτί- σασθε,
πάντες οἱ κατοικοῦντες τὴν οἰκουμένην."6 Τὸ μὲν γὰρ ἀκοῦσαι, κοινὸν ἅπασι τοῖς
ἄπαξ εἰς οὖς λαβοῦσι φωνὴν, ἢ καὶ ἕτερόν τινα κτύπον· τὸ δὲ μὴν ἐνωτίσασθαι, τὸ
εἰς νοῦν, ὡς ἔφην, εἰσοικίσασθαί τι τῶν τεθεσπισμένων. Ἔοικε τοίνυν ὁ προφητικὸς
ἐν τουτοισὶ λόγος τοὺς ἐπιεικέστερον ἤγουν ἐμφρονέ- στερον ἀκροασαμένους
ἐπιζητεῖν, ὥστε καὶ εἰς τὴν τῶν μελλόντων ἀσφάλειαν τὰ τοῖς πάλαι συμβεβηκότα
λαλεῖν. Ὡς γὰρ ὁ Παῦλός φησιν, ὅτι· "6Τὰ τοιάδε τῶν πραγμάτων τυπικῶς
συνέβαινεν ἐκείνοις. Ἐγρά- φη δὲ πρὸς νουθεσίαν ἡμῶν, εἰς οὓς τὰ τέλη τῶν αἰώ-
νων κατήντηκε."6 ∆εῖ γὰρ ἡμᾶς οὐ μάτην τοῖς περὶ αὐτὸν ἐντυγχάνειν διηγήμασιν,
ἀλλ' εἰς ὄνησιν ταῦτα δέχεσθαι ψυχῆς, παραιτεῖσθαι σφόδρα τὸ τοῖς ἴσοις ἁλῶναι
πταίσμασιν, ἵνα μὴ ταῖς ἐκείνων περιπίπτοι- μεν συμφοραῖς. 9Τίς δέ
pass_a_gloss: [...] those from Israel [removed] from the kinship toward God, it has been said clearly, so that God may appear everywhere to have used a just vote. For it was needed, it was needed, that those who honoured the ungodliness toward God come to be outside the sparing and love from him; but that those caught from ignorance in the pits of sin, and having fallen under the devilish hand, be pitied by the Creator of all, being called into knowledge of him and into the light of the truth. For this somewhere is found also through the all-wise Moses, saying: They provoked me to jealousy upon not-gods, they angered me with their carved things. And I will provoke them to jealousy upon a not-nation; upon a senseless nation I will anger them. And the divine Melodist too said somewhere that: They embittered him with their carved things, and with their practices they provoked him to jealousy; and the Lord God saw, and overlooked, and set at nought Israel greatly. And if it is needed to bring some spiritual contemplation too upon the things said, let us guard against having in mind and heart a devilish snare, and the wicked idols in imaginings of thoughts, calling toward licentiousness and into outlandish pleasures, so that we may not become [a prey] to Satan and a plunder of demons. For it is written that: If a spirit of the one holding authority goes up upon you, do not leave your place, because healing will stop great sins. [Lemma, Isaiah 42:23:] Who among you will give ear to these things? Listen into the things coming upon. It is a custom for the God-inspired Scripture to say the 'to give ear' in the case of receiving the word upon the necessary things not by the way, or carelessly, but rather soberly, so as to have the thing told laid up both in mind and heart. Of what sort is the thing said through the voice of the one who sings psalms: In my heart I hid your oracles, so that I may not sin against you. For it is written also in the forty-eighth psalm: Hear these things, all the nations, give ear, all those dwelling in the inhabited world. For to hear is common to all who have once taken into ear a voice, or also some other noise; but to give ear is to settle into the mind, as I said, something of the things decreed. So the prophetic word in these seems to seek those listening more fairly, or more sensibly, so as to tell for the safety of those to come the things that befell those of old. For as Paul says: Such of the things happened to those typically. And they were written for our admonition, into whom the ends of the ages have arrived. For we must not at random come upon the narrations about him, but receive these for benefit of soul, refuse greatly to be caught in the equal faults, so that we may not fall into their misfortunes. [Lemma, Isaiah 42:24:] Who [the section breaks off].
pass_b_english: … the people of Israel from their close bond with God. This has been said plainly, so that God may be seen in every case to have given a just verdict.

For it was necessary, truly necessary, that those who had held ungodliness toward God in honor should be put outside his sparing mercy and love; but that those who through ignorance had been caught in the pits of sin and had fallen under the devil's hand should be pitied by the Creator of all, and called to the knowledge of him and to the light of the truth.

This, I think, is found in the words of the all-wise Moses too, where he says: 'They provoked me to jealousy with what is no god; they angered me with their carved images. And I will provoke them to jealousy with what is no nation; with a senseless nation I will anger them' (Deuteronomy 32:21). And the divine Psalmist said somewhere: 'They embittered him with their carved images, and with their practices they provoked him to jealousy; and the Lord God saw and disregarded them, and utterly rejected Israel' (Psalm 78:58–59; compare Psalm 106:29).

If we should also add some spiritual contemplation to what has been said, let us guard against having the devil's snare in mind and heart, and the wicked idols that arise in the imaginings of our thoughts and call us to licentiousness and to monstrous pleasures, so that we may not fall to Satan and become the plunder of demons. For it is written: 'If the spirit of the ruler rises up against you, do not leave your place, for healing will put an end to great sins' (Ecclesiastes 10:4).
'Who among you will give ear to these things? Listen to what is coming' (Isaiah 42:23).

It is the custom of the divinely inspired Scripture to say 'give ear' when someone receives a word about necessary matters not carelessly or negligently, but soberly, so as to keep what has been told stored up in mind and heart. Such is what is said through the voice of the Psalmist: 'In my heart I have hidden your sayings, so that I may not sin against you' (Psalm 119:11). And in the forty-eighth psalm it is written: 'Hear these things, all you nations; give ear, all who dwell in the world' (Psalm 49:1).
To hear is common to all who have once taken a voice, or some other sound, into the ear; but to give ear is, as I said, to lodge in the mind something of what God has declared.

So the prophetic word here seems to be looking for those who listen more fairly, that is, more wisely, since it tells what befell the people of old for the safety of those to come. As Paul says: 'These things happened to them as types, and they were written for our warning, on whom the ends of the ages have come' (1 Corinthians 10:11). For we must not read the accounts about Israel to no purpose, but receive them for the good of the soul, and firmly refuse to be caught in the same faults, so that we may not fall into the same misfortunes as they did.

choices.english: should be pitied by the Creator of all
choices.why: κατοικτείρω is to pity; the ignorant are shown mercy, not killed.
rejected: were to be killed by the creator of all

choices.why: Cyril's title for David as singer of the Psalms.
rejected: reading Μελῳδός as a proper name

choices.english: If the spirit of the ruler rises up against you
choices.why: The quotation is Ecclesiastes 10:4, used against the devil's assaults.
Cyril distinguishes mere hearing from giving ear, storing the word in mind and heart.
1 Corinthians 10:11: the events of Israel were figures for our warning.
